utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: what's changed

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: nothing

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: what's new

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: same

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: what the patient is actually worried about

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: ABC

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: I hate how you always dismiss my ideas in front of everyone

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Oh please, you do the exact same thing, don't even start

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Name one time! You can't, because it never happens

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Last Tuesday's dinner, ring a bell? You cut me off twice

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: That is completely different and you know it, stop twisting things around

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Am I? Or do you just hate being called out for once in your life?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Why can't you ever just listen instead of turning everything into a fight?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Why can't you admit when you're wrong about something for a change?

summary: Team weighs delaying launch vs hitting marketing dates
title: Product launch debate

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: I think we should push the launch to next month so the onboarding flow is solid

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: But marketing already booked the campaign slots, what would we tell them exactly?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: We tell them a rushed launch hurts more than a delayed one, remember last quarter

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Fair point, though what is the minimum we could ship without embarrassing ourselves?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Probably the core dashboard and the export feature, everything else can wait

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Okay so how do we decide what counts as core versus nice to have here?

summary: Alex walks through the day's plan while Jo mostly listens
title: Morning briefing monologue

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: So the plan for tomorrow is we start with the standup then I will walk through the architecture diagram in detail

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Sounds good

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: After that I need everyone to review the migration checklist I posted yesterday evening carefully

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Will do

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: And please remember the deploy freeze starts Friday so get your pull requests merged before then

summary: Two people mostly saying yeah and uh-huh at each other
title: Backchannel ping-pong

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: So we need to finalize the vendor contract by Friday

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Yeah

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Legal already reviewed the liability clause last week

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Uh-huh

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: The payment terms are net thirty which is standard for us

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Right

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: I told them we need the renewal option in writing

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Mm-hm

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: And the support SLA has to cover weekends during launch

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Yeah

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Procurement wants three competing quotes before sign-off

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Okay

summary: Brief three-turn exchange about the meeting time
title: Quick check-in

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: What time is the client call tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Ten in the morning, same link as last week

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Got it, I will join five minutes early to test audio

summary: Transcript arrived with no speaker labels attached
title: Unlabeled recording

utterances.text: Did anyone pick up the dry cleaning on the way home
I got it, it is hanging by the front door already
Perfect, and did the plumber ever call back about Thursday
No, I will chase him in the morning if we hear nothing
Okay good, let me know what he says about the quote
Will do, it should not take more than a day or two

summary: Doctor sees a patient about three weeks of right knee pain
title: Patient visit - knee pain

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Good morning, what brings you in today?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Morning. It's my right knee, it's been aching for about three weeks now.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: How long has it been bothering you like this, and is it getting worse?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: About three weeks, and definitely worse after my shifts, I'm on my feet all day.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Any swelling, or does it ever lock up on you?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: It swelled up pretty badly last Tuesday, that's when I got worried.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Are you taking anything for it right now?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Just ibuprofen, 400 milligrams when it gets bad in the evening.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: On a scale of one to ten, where is the pain by end of day?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Like a six out of ten by evening, sometimes I can't sleep on that side.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: I'm going to order an X-ray and refer you to physiotherapy to start.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Could this be arthritis? My mother had it quite young.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: We'll see what the imaging shows before we talk about that, no need to jump ahead.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Will I need surgery, do you think?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Let's have you back in three weeks and see how it responds to physio first.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Okay, thank you doctor.

summary: Blood pressure follow-up; dizziness since lisinopril dose increase
title: BP med review

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Morning, Mr. Ellis - you're here for the blood pressure follow-up?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: That's right. Though since you raised the lisinopril to 20 mg, I've been getting dizzy most mornings.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Dizzy how - lightheaded when you stand up, or the room spinning?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Lightheaded standing up. It passes after a minute or two, but it worries me.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Are you taking it every morning, same time?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Every morning with breakfast. I did miss last Thursday, if that matters.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Any swelling, cough, or palpitations since the change?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: No, nothing like that. I do take ibuprofen now and then for my back.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Okay. Readings are still a touch high, so here's the plan: we'll drop the lisinopril back to 10 mg daily and add amlodipine 5 mg.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Should I be worried the dizziness means something serious?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: With the timing it lines up with the dose increase, which is reassuring - but let's get a basic metabolic panel to be thorough.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: And the ibuprofen - keep taking it?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Sparingly, and not on an empty stomach. I'd like to see you back in four weeks to check the new regimen.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Got it. See you then.

summary: School counselor meets a 16-year-old about anxiety and falling asleep in class
title: Teen intake - anxiety

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Thanks for coming in. Your English teacher mentioned you've been falling asleep in class this week. What's going on?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Nothing. I'm just tired.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Tired how? Are you getting enough sleep at night?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: I don't know. I try to sleep but my brain won't shut off.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: What kind of thoughts are keeping you up?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Just... school stuff. Grades. My parents checking my grades. Same stuff.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: That sounds like a lot of pressure. Do your parents fight about school with you?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: They fight with each other mostly. About money. It's loud. I can't concentrate on homework.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: I'm sorry, that must be hard to hear. Is there a place you can go when it gets loud?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: The basement. I have my headphones.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Okay. When you feel that worry ramping up at night, have you tried any calming tricks, like slow breathing?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: No. That stuff doesn't work for me.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Fair enough. Would you be open to trying it just once with me here, and then you can tell me it's useless?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: I guess. Whatever.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Breathe in for four counts, hold for four, out for four. We'll do two rounds.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: It was... okay. A little quieter.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: A little quieter is a win. I'd like to check in weekly while things at home are rough. Same time next Tuesday?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Sure.

summary: First addiction-counseling session: client describes online sports betting, chasing losses, and hiding it from his partner
title: Counseling intake - gambling

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Welcome in. What made you decide to book this appointment?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: My wife found the credit card statement. Three months of bets I told her I quit.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: That took courage to come here anyway. What kind of betting has it been?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Mostly sports. Online. Started with the playoff run last year, twenty bucks a game, that felt normal.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: When did it stop feeling normal?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: When I lost eight hundred on a Sunday and put down twelve hundred Monday to win it back. You know how that goes.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Chasing losses. How deep did it get?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: About nine grand on the card. I borrowed two from my brother to cover the minimums.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Have you been able to stay away from it since your wife found out?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: ...I reinstalled the app Thursday. Deleted it again Friday. That's what scares me.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: The pull is stronger than your plan. That's the cycle, not a character flaw. What triggers it most?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Boredom, honestly. Night shift weeks, everyone asleep, the phone's right there.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: What would you want to look like six months from now if this went well?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Debt gone. My wife trusting me with the bills again. Not checking the lines at 2 a.m.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Those are real, achievable goals. I'd like to see you weekly and talk about a self-exclusion plan for the apps. Does Thursday work?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Thursday works. I need this to stick.

summary: First counseling session: client describes nightly online shopping binges, hidden packages, and two maxed-out credit cards
title: Counseling intake - shopping

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Thanks for coming in. Tell me a little about why you're here today.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: I can't stop buying things. I told myself I'd stop last month and I ordered four more things Tuesday night.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: What does a typical evening look like when that happens?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Kids are in bed, I'm exhausted, and I start scrolling. It feels relaxing at first, like I'm treating myself.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: And then?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Then it's three in the morning and I've bought two hundred dollars of stuff I don't remember wanting. That's when the panic starts.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Do the people at home know about the purchases?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: I have packages sent to the car trunk now. My husband asked about a box last week and I lied and said it was a gift.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Hiding them. That must be stressful to carry. What's the financial picture right now?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: Two cards nearly maxed. About eleven thousand total. I keep returning things to feel in control but the returns don't cover it.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: The returns are interesting - it sounds like part of you knows these aren't real needs. What need IS underneath, do you think?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: I think... I'm so drained from work and the kids that buying something is the only part of my day that feels like it's mine.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: That's honest and important. What could a part of the day that's yours look like, without the credit card?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: I used to paint. I haven't touched the watercolors in two years.

utterances.speaker: Speaker 1
utterances.text: Maybe that's a door back. Let's meet weekly, and between now and next time, one small step: delete one shopping app from your phone. Can you pick one?

utterances.speaker: Speaker 2
utterances.text: The worst one. I'll delete it tonight.
